faq.a: Twelve calculators: what is X% of Y; X is what percent of Y; percentage increase/decrease; add or subtract X% from a value; reverse percentage (find the original before a change); percentage difference (relative to the average); aggregate marks across multiple subjects; percentage to fraction/decimal/ratio; CGPA↔percentage; discount (and reverse discount from two prices); GST-style add/remove; and profit & loss from cost and selling price.

faq.q: Does it show how each answer is calculated?
faq.a: Yes. Every result displays the formula with your numbers filled in — for example reverse percentage shows "final ÷ (1 − p/100)", and marks shows "(obtained ÷ total) × 100". This is handy for writing out working in an exam. Each calculation is also added to a history list (last 25) saved in your browser, and results have a copy button.

faq.q: How does the CGPA to percentage conversion work?
faq.a: It multiplies CGPA by a factor you can change, defaulting to 9.5 (the CBSE convention), so percentage = CGPA × 9.5 and the reverse divides by the same factor. Because the factor is editable, you can match whatever formula your own university uses. The tool labels it as a common university formula rather than a universal standard.

faq.q: Are there shortcuts for competitive-exam maths?
faq.a: Yes. A reference grid lists common fraction-to-percentage equivalents (1/3 = 33.33%, 1/8 = 12.5%, and so on), plus mental-maths tips like x% of y = y% of x, and the rule that successive changes of a% and b% give a net of a + b + (a·b)/100. Everything runs in your browser with nothing sent to a server.
